svg.title: A Python signature becomes a JSON Schema
svg.desc: On the left, the decorated Python function find_process, whose parameters are name annotated as str with no default and limit annotated as int with a default of 25. On the right, the JSON Schema the software development kit generated from that signature, reproduced exactly as it appears on the wire, from the opening brace through the properties for name and limit to the required list and the title find_processArguments. Two stepped leader lines connect each parameter to the property it became, and a coloured key marks the name lines in one colour and the limit lines in another. A panel under the code notes the two things the leader lines do not cover: the docstring becomes the tool's description and the return type becomes outputSchema. Two panels along the bottom state the rule the figure exists to teach: no default means the parameter is required and a client that omits it gets an error instead of a result, while a default means the value appears as a default keyword and the name stays out of required. A closing line says four type hints cover almost everything: str, int, float and bool become string, integer, number and boolean.
svg.text: You write the signature; the SDK writes the schema
The object on the right was generated from the function on the left and is reproduced exactly as it goes over the wire.
The parts the leader lines do not cover
The docstring becomes the tool's description.
The return type becomes outputSchema. Post 06.
No default, so the parameter is required
A client that omits it gets an error instead of a result.
A default, so the parameter is optional
The value appears as default, and the name stays out of required.
Four type hints cover almost everything: str, int, float and bool become string, integer, number and boolean.
